title: Reserve lanes credit expiry and proactive invoice communication
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using reserved/dedicated lanes with temporary credits (on-demand reserve lanes / surge credits) are surprised when short-lived credit allocations expire and trigger immediate overage charges. This causes support tickets and churn for mid-market customers who rely on predictable billing.

Scope: Implement a reserve-lane credit expiry policy plus proactive invoice communication and UI affordances so customers understand: remaining credit, expiry time, how overage will be billed, and mitigations (grace window, auto-extend, or manual top-up). This ticket covers runtime accounting changes, billing ledger tagging, console UI copy/indicator, and an outbound invoice-preview notification flow.

Goals:
- Define deterministic credit TTL and decay semantics for reserve lanes used as temporary boosts.
- Prevent immediate hard-cut overage surprises by adding a configurable grace window and invoice-preview system.
- Surface credit expiry and likely invoice impact in the Console and via email/webhook 24 hours before expiry.
- Ensure accounting is auditable: every boost allocation and expiry must produce ledger entries with reason codes for invoices and support.

Non-goals: Changes to long-term reserved capacity (monthly commits) billing rules; price changes to overage rates.

Background/context: Our existing surge/boost implementation allocates ephemeral capacity from surge pools and tracks credits only at allocation time. When the credit expires we currently allow requests to fall back to host pricing immediately, which can create sharp invoice spikes. Prior tickets around surge accounting (see dependencies) debated amortized vs instantaneous invoicing; this ticket operationalizes a middle-ground: short grace + clear communication.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic credit TTL is implemented (default 48 hours) and configurable per-boost allocation by the platform team.
A billing ledger change logs boost_start, boost_end, grace_period_start, and overage_transition with timestamp and reason codes.
Console shows: remaining boost credit (tokens/minute), expiry ETA, estimated invoice impact if not extended, and an action to extend/top-up.
Automatic invoice-preview emails/webhooks are emitted 24 hours and 2 hours before expiry containing estimated overage and recommended actions.
E2E tests validating: allocations expire correctly, grace window behavior prevents immediate invoice jumps, and ledger entries match expected transitions.
Docs updated: billing FAQ + runbook for Support with reproducible steps and example ledger entries.
Performance: expiry and ledger writes do not add >20ms tail latency to allocation control plane operations under normal load.

risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers could extend repeatedly to avoid overage which increases capacity pressure. Mitigation: add throttle on auto-extend via policy (max 3 extensions per 30 days) and surface cost estimate clearly.

Risk: Ledger migration for active boosts may cause temporary double-billing if done incorrectly. Mitigation: migration runs in read-only mode first; reconciliation script included and tested in staging.
Risk: Notification spam. Mitigation: notification preferences respect account-level settings; only customers with active boosts receive preview emails.
Risk: Attack vector where non-privileged actors trigger many short boosts to cause ledger churn. Mitigation: allocation rate-limit per account and owner-level quota checks.
implementation_notes: Allocator: store boost metadata with allocation_id, expiry_ts, and decay_policy. Expiry worker moves allocation from BOOST_ACTIVE -> BOOST_GRACE -> OVERAGE with single ledger emission per transition.
Billing: new ledger events (boost_start/end/grace_start/overage_transition) added to schema. Each event includes estimated_cost_delta field for invoice preview generation.
Console: new UI elements call /v1/dedicated/allocations/{id}/preview to compute estimated invoice if not extended. Preview is cached for 5 minutes.
Notifications: queue-based delivery via notifications-service; supports email and webhook channels. Templates in /docs/templates/invoice-preview/.
Feature flags: rolling rollout behind "reserve_lanes_expiry_v1" and expiry_batching as mentioned by SRE.
